newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to provide $400 mln for Calif. rail project.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to provide $400 mln for Calif. rail project.

text.p: Federal officials on Friday will announce an agreement to provide up to $400 million in federal loans to the Alameda Corridor project, a southern California rail and highway freight transportation system.

Secretary of Transportation Federico Pena, Federal Highway Administrator Rodney Slater and the mayors of Long Beach and Los Angeles will hold a press conference later Friday to discuss the federal loan for the $1.9 billion project.
The Department of Transportation said in a statement that it planned to distribute toward the project up to $400 million in loan funds over three years, beginning in 1997.

The $1.9 billion Alameda Corridor is expected to improve rail operations linking the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach to shippers throughout North America, Los Angeles and Long Beach officials say.
The two ports handle one-fourth of all U.S. waterborne international trade and are linked to 2.5 million jobs.
